question.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.9),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}(0.2)^{x-1}(0.8), & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are infinitely many values of $X$ such that $X>3.$ However, we can simplify the computation by using the complement instead:

$$
P(X>3)=1-P(X\le 3)
$$

Computing the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =P(X\in \{1,2,3\}) \\  & =P(X=1)+P(X=2)+P(X=3) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3) \\  & =(0.2)^{0}(0.8)+(0.2)^{1}(0.8)+(0.2)^{2}(0.8) \\  & =0.992.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>3) & =1-P(X\le 3) \\  & =1-0.992 \\  & =0.008.\end{aligned}
$$
